title: OmniPrep™ For High Quality Genomic DNA Extraction From Plant Tissue
author: G-Biosciences
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.e6dbha6
materials: Allow the sample to cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Freeze and grind tissue
steps.instruction: Freeze plant tissue in liquid nitrogen and grind to a fine powder.

steps.title: Add tissue to lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Add 50–100 mg of the finely ground dried, frozen, or fresh leaf tissue to a microcentrifuge tube containing 500 µl Genomic Lysis Buffer.

steps.title: Homogenize lysate
steps.instruction: If the tissue is already ground, vortex the tube for 5 seconds; if not, homogenize with a microfuge pestle for approximately 30–60 strokes until a homogeneous suspension is obtained.

steps.title: Incubate lysate
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 65 °C for 60 minutes, inverting the tube periodically.

steps.title: Add chloroform
steps.instruction: Add 200 µl chloroform to the tube and mix by inverting the tube several times.

steps.title: Phase separation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 10 minutes at 14,000 × g, then carefully transfer the upper aqueous phase to a clean microcentrifuge tube.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the upper aqueous phase to a clean microcentrifuge tube

steps.title: Add DNA stripping solution
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl DNA Stripping Solution to the aqueous phase and invert several times to mix.

steps.title: Heat stripping mixture
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture for 5–10 minutes at 60 °C.

steps.title: Add precipitation solution
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl Precipitation Solution and invert the tube several times; a white precipitate should appear. If no precipitate forms, add 50 µl aliquots of Precipitation Solution until a white precipitate is observed.

steps.title: Centrifuge precipitate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 14,000 × g for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Isopropanol DNA precipitation
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a clean tube, add 500 µl isopropanol to precipitate genomic DNA, and invert the tube 10 times to mix.

steps.title: Add glycogen (optional)
steps.instruction: Optionally add 2 µl Mussel Glycogen as a DNA carrier to improve recovery.

steps.title: Pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14,000 × g for 5 minutes to pellet the genomic DNA, then discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA pellet with 70 % ethanol and centrifuge.

substeps.instruction: Add 700 µl 70 % ethanol to the pellet and invert several times

steps.title: Dry pellet
steps.instruction: Remove ethanol and dry the pellet briefly.

substeps.instruction: Decant or pipette off the ethanol wash
Invert the tube on a clean absorbent surface for several minutes to drain excess ethanol; avoid letting the pellet dry completely

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl TE Buffer to the pellet and incubate at room temperature for at least 15 minutes to rehydrate (incubation at 55–60 °C for 5–60 minutes can be used to speed rehydration).

steps.title: RNase treatment (optional)
steps.instruction: Optionally add 1 µl LongLife™ RNase per 100 µl TE Buffer now.

steps.title: Store DNA
steps.instruction: Store the DNA solution at 4 °C for short‑term use; for long‑term storage keep at –20 °C or –80 °C. Typical yield is 0.5–3 µg per mg of plant tissue.
